item.title: IBM Says Second-Quarter Sales Missed as Customers Pulled Back
item.description: International Business Machines Corp. reported preliminary quarterly sales results that missed analysts estimates with Chief Executive Officer Arvind Krishna saying customers were holding back spending. The shares dropped.

item.title: Famitsu at 40: Conspiracies, Clicks and the Future of Gaming Media
item.description: The weekly publication wears its love of games proudly

item.title: Hong Kong, Onetime Mecca for Capitalism, Adopts Five-Year Planning
item.description: Hong Kong is adopting its first “five-year plan,” closely aligning it with mainland objectives.

item.title: Nebius to Sell $1 Billion in AI Capacity to Startup Reflection
item.description: Cloud provider Nebius Group NV agreed to sell more than $1 billion worth of computing power to Reflection AI, a developer of artificial intelligence models that was launched by two former Google DeepMind researchers.

item.title: DeepSeek Mulls New Funding Weeks After $7 Billion Round, FT Says
item.description: Chinese AI pioneer DeepSeek is considering raising more funds weeks after closing a $7 billion round of financing, the Financial Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the deal.

item.title: China Solar Giant Longi Green Sees Deeper First-Half Loss
item.description: Longi Green Energy Technology Co. expects its net loss to widen in the first half, despite a surge in solar exports earlier in the year.

item.title: SLB, Liberty Energy to Sell Power and Parts to Data Centers
item.description: SLB, the world’s largest oil field service provider, has agreed to partner with Liberty Energy Inc. to provide modular parts and power for data centers, the latest example of energy companies positioning themselves to benefit from the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Fed Is Behind The Curve as Tech Economy Booms, TS Lombard Says
item.description: The Federal Reserve should start tightening policy to constrain the artificial intelligence boom gripping the US, TS Lombard Chief Economist Freya Beamish said.

item.title: Hormuz Tensions Put Commodity Supplies at Risk Far Beyond Oil
item.description: The latest flare-up of tensions over the Strait of Hormuz is threatening fresh global supply disruptions way beyond oil and gas.

item.title: Thailand Scraps Plan to End Visa-Free Entry for Indian Tourists
item.description: Thailand will allow 30-day visa-exempted entries by visitors from India, after a proposal to scrap visa-free entry led arrivals from the South Asian nation to drop in a blow to the vital tourism industry.

item.title: China Urges Normal Hormuz Passage as Trump Reinstates Blockade
item.description: China called for restoring normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz as soon as possible after President Donald Trump reinstated the US blockade of Iranian ships transiting through the vital waterway.

item.title: Rate Hike Chances Rising as Warsh Takes Center Stage
item.description: Following a spike in oil prices and hawkish commentary from Fed officials, traders see a nearly 50% chance of a July rate hike.

item.title: Germany Sees Economy Stabilizing as New Fighting Clouds Outlook
item.description: Germany’s government said the economy is showing signs of stabilizing even as renewed hostilities in the Middle East could yet derail an expected recovery in the second half.

item.title: Emerging Assets Steady as Middle East Tensions Spur Caution
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies were little changed as investors turned cautious amid escalating tensions in the Middle East and awaited the latest US inflation report for clues on the path of monetary policy.

item.title: How Brands Sneak In Cheaper Ingredients to Protect Their Profit Margins
item.description: Companies are enlisting consultants and spending millions to reformulate their most beloved products.

item.title: Fed’s Three Picks for Task Force Show AI Bullishness
item.description: Kevin Warsh has argued AI could allow the economy to expand faster without generating as much inflation.

item.title: Polish Rate Hike More Likely Than Cut, MPC’s Zarzecki Says
item.description: The Polish central bank’s next interest rate move is more likely to be an increase rather than the cut suggested by Governor Adam Glapinski, according to another member of the Monetary Policy Council.

item.title: Deutsche Bank’s Saravelos Says Pound Buoyed by Burnham Rhetoric
item.description: Pound traders will be looking for fresh catalysts after a rally in the run-up to Andy Burnham’s expected move into 10 Downing Street, according to Deutsche Bank AG’s George Saravelos.

item.title: Lead Drops as LME Inventories Surge the Most Since at Least 1970
item.description: Lead prices dropped after the biggest delivery into London Metal Exchange warehouses in records going back to 1970.

item.title: Shell Gets More Tax Relief on $20 Billion Nigerian Oil Project
item.description: Nigeria granted Shell Plc a production-linked tax credit for a deepwater project, an incentive that will be offered to other oil majors as Africa’s biggest producer seeks to boost production, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Job Hunters Are Using AI to Cheat in Interviews, and Failing at the Office
item.description: This has left managers paranoid — and scrambling to reverse course.

item.title: Polymarket Partners With Crypto Firm During World Cup Semifinals
item.description: Crypto brokerage Blockchain.com Group Holdings Inc. has partnered with Polymarket to offer prediction markets to its users in time for the World Cup semifinals.

item.title: US Small-Business Optimism Rises by Most in More Than a Year
item.description: An index of US small business optimism rose in June by the most in more than a year as lower oil prices offered firms some relief.

item.title: Chile Economic Euphoria Crashes to Earth as President Kast Faces 1% Growth
item.description: Chileans elected a pro-market president to revive the economy. They are now getting a reality check as one of Latin America’s richest nations flirts with recession while a rightward regional shift heralds more competition for investment.

item.title: Ethiopian Air Studies Large Order That Puts Jet Rivals in Play
item.description: Ethiopian Airlines Group is in the final stages of deciding on an aircraft order for as many as 50 jets, as Africa’s largest carrier looks to renew its fleet and expand its foothold on the continent.

item.title: India Refiners Reap Fuel Export Windfall as War Drives Shortages
item.description: Oil-product shipments from India are on track to climb to their highest level since September as refiners cash in on robust profit margins after a Russian export ban and hostilities in the Middle East tightened supplies.

item.title: Deutsche Bank May Win Russia Sanctions Lawsuit Against Linde
item.description: Deutsche Bank AG may win a legal battle in a dispute with a corporate client over who has to pick up the tap for losses linked to sanctions on Russia, according to a German court.

item.title: Credit Suisse Veteran Becomes Lunate-Backed Firm’s Abu Dhabi CEO
item.description: Azura Partners, a wealth advisor backed by one of the Middle East’s largest alternative asset managers, named Credit Suisse veteran Yousef Hajjar to oversee its Abu Dhabi operations.

item.title: PBOC Boosts Liquidity to Smooth Tax Payments, Debt Issuance
item.description: China’s central bank said it’s boosting longer-term liquidity injections through outright reverse repurchase agreements, a move expected to help companies and individuals handle upcoming tax payments and to sustain demand for debt issuance.

item.title: ECB Digital Euro Trial Enlists Firms from Revolut to UniCredit
item.description: Revolut Bank UAB, UniCredit SpA and Deutsche Bank AG are among 36 payment service providers that will participate in a digital euro trial, the European Central Bank said on Tuesday.
